+def _regexp_transformer(value: str) -> Pattern[str]:
+    """Return `re.compile(value)`, falling back to the `regex` module.
+
+    The `regex` module is used, if available, to compile the pattern
+    whenever `re.compile` raises a `re.error`. This makes it possible to use
+    extended regular expression syntax not supported by the standard
+    library, e.g. ``\\p{Han}``, while still using ``re`` (and returning a
+    standard ``re.Pattern``) whenever possible.
+    """
+    try:
+        return re.compile(value)
+    except re.error as ex:
+        if not HAS_REGEX_MODULE:
+            raise
+        try:
+            return regex.compile(value)  # type: ignore[return-value]
+        except regex.error:
+            # Raise the original ``re.error`` so callers relying on this
+            # exception type (or its ``sre_constants.error`` alias) still
+            # observe consistent behaviour for genuinely invalid patterns.
+            raise ex from None
